solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Setter's to work on parking that's not smooth

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the setter says I'm, short for I am
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: A crossword setter is put to work on a car park whose surface is rough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the setter and the work after the parking letter. 'Setter's' is setter is, which the setter would say as I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimply face is covered in spots, so its skin is bumpy rather than smooth.

clue.text: Heartless gang showing attitude

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter

blocks.note: a posse is a gang, originally one gathered by a sheriff

explanation.surface: A violent gang with no compassion displays a menacing attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the middle S of the five-letter gang leaves POSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pose is a bodily stance or an adopted manner, both senses of attitude.

clue.text: Transform Ibiza after removing business for hypnotic drug

indicators.note: removing means taking some letters out of the island's name

blocks.note: to morph is to transform
the Spanish island, taken as written
biz is slang for business

explanation.surface: Clubbers transform Ibiza, once the business is gone, into a place for a sleep-inducing drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Ibiza is the Balearic party island; the clue uses its name as raw letters, not as a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Morphia is an old name for morphine, an opiate that induces sleep.

clue.text: First of twin boys penning New Year's letter

indicators.note: to pen something is to enclose it, as in a sheep pen

blocks.note: twin boys are two lads; this is the first of them
N is the abbreviation for new
the second of the two lads
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: The elder of two twin boys writes a New Year's letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The first LAD holds N to make LAND; the second LAD takes Y to make LADY. 'Letter' is not post but one who lets, a classic crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlady lets rooms or property to tenants, so she is literally a letter.

clue.text: Steel transducer backfired in musical instrument

indicators.note: something that backfires goes the wrong way, so the word runs backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: a microphone, mic for short, turns sound into electrical signals
the sitar is the long-necked Indian lute

explanation.surface: A sound transducer failed noisily inside a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel' looks like the metal, perhaps of a steel guitar, but is poetic for a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel stands for a sword in literary use, and a scimitar is a curved oriental sword.

clue.text: One with eyes only for the TV?

definitions.text: One with eyes only for the TV?

blocks.clueFragment: One with eyes only for the TV?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who cannot stop watching television
setter's reading: a tuber's buds are its eyes, so the vegetable itself has them

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the lazy viewer is a kind of potato, and potatoes really do have eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch potato is an idler who spends hours slumped on the sofa watching television.

clue.text: Mowed a tricky area of grassland

indicators.note: something tricky is intricate and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cut the grass on an awkward patch of field.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a field of grass, often kept for hay.

clue.text: A lame youngster needs support around and provisions at this point

indicators.note: around says the support is wrapped about the other piece

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
taken as written
Tiny Tim is the crippled boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: A disabled child needs help moving about and supplies brought to him.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiny Tim, the crippled boy in Dickens's A Christmas Carol, is the stock lame youngster. The definition is a whole phrase: the hour at which food is laid on.
explanation.definitionFit: Teatime is the time of day when tea and a light meal are served, so provisions arrive then.

clue.text: Party animal retires or crashes

indicators.note: a crash leaves things smashed and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard partier either goes home to bed or collapses in a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A roisterer is a noisy reveller, which is what party animal means colloquially.

clue.text: After ignoring her absolutely, Italian woman's pulled back skirt

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving some letters out of the woman's title
pulled back means drawn the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: signora is Italian for a married woman, plus the S of the possessive
her emphatic yes, in Italian, is si

explanation.surface: An Italian lady, having brushed off a woman's yes, hitches up her skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNORAS loses SI to leave GNORAS, which is then read backwards. Si is Italian for yes, which the clue renders as 'absolutely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist as a skirt, worn in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Recalled one sailor with a vessel that's spouted exotic language

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the string is read in the backward direction

blocks.note: the Roman numeral one
a tar is an old word for a sailor
with links on the article, taken as written
a jug is a vessel for pouring

explanation.surface: A sailor remembers a spouted pitcher that came from a far-off land.
explanation.walkthrough: I, TAR, A and JUG are run together and the whole is reversed. 'Spouted' does double duty in the surface for the jug but serves as part of the link to 'language'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gujarati is the language of Gujarat in western India, exotic to a British solver.

clue.text: Greek character halts on trip that's difficult – he's good to us

indicators.note: a difficult trip is a rough one, and the letters are jolted into a new order

blocks.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A Greek stops on an arduous journey to help others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' sounds like a person from Greece but means a letter. 'Us' in the definition stands for humanity at large.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanthropist gives generously to benefit mankind, so he is kind to all of us.

clue.text: Items to fix office chair broken by ultimately careless presenters

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final letter of the next word
broken by means split open with something pushed into the gap

blocks.note: replacement wheels for a chair are new casters
the last letter of careless

explanation.surface: Parts to repair a desk chair were damaged by a slapdash TV presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: Casters are the small swivelling wheels under an office chair; the single letter splits the two words of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Newscasters read the news on radio or television, so they are broadcast presenters.

clue.text: Exert pressure towards mass of hair that hurts soon after scratching head

indicators.note: scratching out the head means the first letter is struck off

blocks.note: a beard is a mass of facial hair
ow is the cry of pain
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: Scratching a sore, itchy beard makes one push down hard on it.
explanation.walkthrough: ANON without its first letter gives NON. 'Exert pressure towards' would read better as one phrase, but the definition is the verb phrase and 'towards' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear down on is to press heavily on something or advance threateningly upon it.

clue.text: One informing wife to tuck into exploded sausage

indicators.note: tucking something into another places it inside

blocks.note: a thing that exploded has burst
a rat is an informer
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An informer's wife digs into a sausage that has split in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploded' looks like an anagram signal but supplies a word, and 'tuck into' suggests eating rather than insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A bratwurst is a German pork sausage, usually fried or grilled.

clue.text: Dieter respectfully addressed that woman with posterior twice the norm

blocks.note: her is the pronoun for that woman
her rear letter appears twice instead of once

explanation.surface: A slimmer is politely spoken to by a woman with a very large bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dieter' is not a slimmer but a German man's name. The final letter of HER is doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is the German title for a man, equivalent to Mr, used when addressing someone politely.

clue.text: Cowboy's hit and run

definitions.note: noun in the clue used attributively, as in cowboy builders; the answer is an adjective

blocks.note: a slap is a hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: A Wild West cowboy strikes someone and flees.
explanation.walkthrough: A cowboy in British slang is a shoddy, unqualified tradesman, not a cattle herder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowboy work is careless and slipshod, which is what slapdash describes.

clue.text: How belated message might be given for native Africans?

blocks.note: as means in the way that, or how
a PS, postscript, is added after the letter is finished

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a late note could be passed to Africans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native Africans' sounds like people, but means snakes native to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are venomous snakes, the Egyptian cobra and others, found across Africa.

clue.text: Dial-a-motorcyclist provides stylish carriage

blocks.note: dial and pan are both slang for the face
taken as written
Che Guevara toured South America by motorbike in The Motorcycle Diaries

explanation.surface: A call-out motorbike service offers a smart vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dial-a-' looks like a phone service but splits into face, A and a famous rider.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache is flamboyant style, a confident way of carrying oneself.

clue.text: Craft alien once abandoned by river

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An alien spacecraft was once left beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoned' reads as left behind, but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship, a seagoing vessel or craft.

clue.text: Mollycoddled orphan in case of need

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the first and last letters of need
Little Orphan Annie, heroine of the comic strip and the musical Annie

explanation.surface: An orphan was spoilt whenever she was in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as circumstance, as in 'in case of', but means the outside letters of the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny someone is to fuss over them like a nurse, so nannied means overprotected.

clue.text: Only one pound in dollars exchanged back

definitions.note: noun in the clue; the answer is the adjective, of the back

indicators.note: only one means a doubled letter keeps a single copy
exchanged means swapped about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: L, from the Latin libra, stands for a pound
taken as written

explanation.surface: A currency dealer gets only a single pound for his dollars and hands them back.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for American money has two Ls; drop one and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorsal means relating to the back, as in a fish's dorsal fin.

clue.text: Operating system working with half of resources, as browser is doing

blocks.note: Windows is Microsoft's operating system
getting about on one leg uses only half of your legs

explanation.surface: A computer system running on half its resources, as a web browser does.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing surface misleads twice: the browser is a person idly looking in shops, not software.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser in a shop looks at goods without buying, which is what window-shopping is.

clue.text: What might be delivered by pumps in industrial estate

definitions.text: What might be delivered by pumps

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the boundary of the two words

explanation.surface: Something produced by pumps on a factory site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pumps' suggests machinery, but these are bar handpumps that draw beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ales are beers, pulled from the cask by a bar's handpumps.

clue.text: Secret places SS put beside sports field

blocks.note: the rec is short for recreation ground
two letter S written out in words are esses

explanation.surface: Hidden spots where the SS were posted next to a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'SS' suggests the Nazi corps but asks for the letter's name spelt out, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Recesses are hidden or remote nooks, as in the recesses of the mind.

clue.text: Almost yielding to accept a beauty treatment

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter goes
to accept is to take something in

blocks.note: facile can mean pliant or easily led
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nearly giving in and agreeing to a beauty treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: FACILE shortened to FACIL takes A before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A facial is a salon treatment cleansing and massaging the face.

clue.text: Fish trapped in lock pines with others missing

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside something else

blocks.note: a tress is a lock of hair
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish caught in a canal lock pines for its absent companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pines' reads as a verb of longing, but it is trees, and with every other tree gone the place is bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Treeless land has no trees at all, pines or any other kind.

clue.text: Island on which one travels by trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for the mouth, so this comes by word of mouth

blocks.note: highways are what one travels along

explanation.surface: An island where people get about in a pony and trap.
explanation.walkthrough: A trap is both a horse-drawn cart and slang for the mouth; the second sense signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is the largest of the Dodecanese islands in the Aegean.
